role: biostatistician (D2 evidence for decision impact, D8 added value over alternatives, path to viability)

scores.reason: Consensus/review text (ADA/EASD 2021 adult T1D report; Jones and Hattersley 2013; ADA Standards 2026 section 2 per project file) supports random C-peptide for classifying long-duration or doubtful-type insulin-treated adults, backed by cohort accuracy data. No trial or outcome study of C-peptide-guided insulin withdrawal was found; the only retrieved de-escalation-adjacent study (Funakoshi 2011) is retrospective with likelihood ratios about 2, so the stop-insulin decision itself would score 2. Measure type: random/non-fasting C-peptide with concurrent glucose.
sources: PMID 34593612 DOI 10.2337/dci21-0043 abstract (consensus; content on C-peptide taken from project file, not read by me)
PMID 41358893 DOI 10.2337/dc26-s002 abstract only (full text read level per project file only)

scores.reason: Alternatives within the population (insulin-treated, doubtful type, at least 3 years) are clinical features, islet autoantibodies and type 1 genetic risk score; these predict type but not residual insulin secretion. C-peptide is the direct measure and is the reference standard in the UK model studies, so its incremental value over the alternatives was never quantified (no C-statistic/NRI or reclassification rate found). Mechanism and consensus text only, so capped at 2 under anchor 19.
sources: PMID 31558459 DOI 10.1136/bmjopen-2019-031586 abstract (C-peptide used as outcome definition, not predictor)

scores.reason: A systematic review with expert recommendations (PMDI 2023) and an ANZ 2025 consensus statement set out who to test, and the latter endorses validated probability tools; UCPCR accuracy studies and an externally validated biomarker-inclusive calculator (2026) support C-peptide as a triage component. No study shows that C-peptide-based triage raises diagnostic yield versus clinical criteria in a prospective pathway, and PPV of the antibody-negative UCPCR-positive pathway was 20 percent (project file). Measure type: random/post-meal blood C-peptide or UCPCR.
sources: PMID 37794142 DOI 10.1038/s43856-023-00369-8 abstract (full text read per project file only)

scores.reason: In early-insulin-treated people (the T1D-proxy group) adding C-peptide and autoantibodies to clinical features raised ROC AUC from 0.80 (95% CrI 0.71-0.82) to 0.98 (0.95-0.98), with external validation; biomarkers alone gave 0.96. This shows the biomarker pair changes the answer, but the C-peptide contribution is not separated from antibodies, and UCPCR cannot separate MODY from type 2 diabetes (AUC 0.57 in children; 0.2 nmol/mmol cutoff separates MODY from T1D over 5 years: 97% sensitivity, 96% specificity, adults).

The Endocrine Society 2009 guideline (GRADE, evidence graded low to very low) recommends measuring glucose, insulin, C-peptide and circulating oral hypoglycaemic agents during an episode. The project file states insulin and C-peptide show only the hyperinsulinaemic pattern, identical to insulinoma, and that no accuracy data were retrieved; the drug screen is the discriminating test. So evidence for the insulin/C-peptide contribution to the sulfonylurea decision is observational or expert only. Measure type: insulin and C-peptide measured during hypoglycaemia (fasting/spontaneous).
sources: usecases-verified.md row 3 (Cryer 2009 abstract; PES 2015 full text per project file)

scores.reason: Plasma or urine drug screen discriminates sulfonylurea/meglitinide from insulinoma; insulin and C-peptide add only confirmation of endogenous hyperinsulinism and exclusion of exogenous insulin (low C-peptide). No retrieved data show insulin/C-peptide changing the answer beyond the screen, and the screen can miss newer agents (project file).

Evidence is observational: one prospective single-centre-network cohort (n=294 DKA patients, 12-60 months follow-up; Abeta scheme sensitivity 99.4, specificity 95.9, LR+ 24.6, AUC 0.972 for later preserved beta-cell function) and an n=103 cohort showing persistent insulin requirement in beta-negative groups. The accuracy outcome is itself defined by glucagon-stimulated C-peptide at 12 months, so it is partly circular. No guideline recommending the test and no trial of C-peptide-guided insulin withdrawal were found in the screened records. Measure type: glucagon-stimulated or fasting C-peptide after DKA resolution.

In the 294-patient cohort the scheme combining autoantibodies and beta-cell function (C-peptide) was the most accurate of four schemes against immunologic only, immunologic plus insulin requirement, and BMI schemes (comparator figures were in the truncated part of the abstract and were not read). Autoantibodies and BMI alone mislabel ketosis-prone diabetes, so C-peptide adds beyond them. Downgraded confidence because of circular outcome definition and single research network; one population (largely Afro-Caribbean and African American patients).
scores.correction: Full-text review FT16 (2026-10-26; skeptic-checked in usecases/scoring/ft-review/skeptic-FT15-17.md; applied with the user's approval): D8 3 to 2. Balasubramanyam 2006 (PMID 17130187, DOI 10.2337/dc06-0749; full text): the AUC 0.972 is partly circular (the outcome is the same glucagon C-peptide test that defines the scheme) and the same group's 2008 review (PMID 18292467, DOI 10.1210/er.2007-0026) says the cut-offs do not independently predict safe insulin withdrawal; V6 had already asked for this downgrade.

scores.reason: The fasting C-peptide below 0.6 ng/mL criterion is a Japan Diabetes Society expert definition (2023); the abstract gives no derivation or validation of the cutoff. Supporting observational data: TIDE-J cohort (n=314; 9.1 percent of slowly progressive cases reached undetectable C-peptide by 5 years) and a 60-patient Japanese database study using 0.6 ng/mL to define progressors. No outcome or decision-impact study. Measure type: fasting C-peptide.
sources: PMID 38184802 DOI 10.1111/jdi.14121 abstract (full text read by project skeptic only)

scores.reason: Within the population (autoantibody-positive, non-ketotic at diagnosis, on insulin beyond 3 months) insulin treatment itself is already part of the definition, so C-peptide adds a severity/definite-versus-probable label. In the 60-patient study fasting C-peptide, age, BMI, GADA titre and IA-2A all raised the PPV for progression (from about 56-72 percent to 77-84 percent) but C-peptide contribution over insulin requirement was not tested. Mechanism and one small study only.

Observational prognostic cohort evidence only: DPTRS (OGTT glucose and C-peptide sums, fasting C-peptide, age, BMI) was developed in DPT-1 and externally validated in TrialNet; 2-year risk after the 9.00 threshold was 0.88 (DPT-1) and 0.77 (TrialNet). Index60 thresholds are medians of progressors applied to the full cohorts (replication, not independent validation). The 2015 staging statement says staging is not recommended for clinical practice and found baseline insulin sensitivity, fasting insulin secretion and total postglucose insulin output not predictive, and no guideline recommends C-peptide testing; whether monitoring intensity guided by these scores changes outcomes is untested. Measure type: post-load (OGTT) C-peptide with glucose; not fasting insulin.
sources: PMID 39992257 DOI 10.1210/clinem/dgaf086 abstract (truncated; Table 3 per project file)

scores.reason: DPTRS 9.00 (glucose plus C-peptide) identified 2-year risk of 0.77-0.88, versus 0.37 after dysglycaemia first appeared in DPT-1, so the combined score outperforms glucose-based staging; but no incremental C-statistic or NRI of C-peptide over antibody number, glucose and age was found. In a 57-person multivariable model AUC C-peptide was not significant (OR 0.999, P=.330) while oral-minimal-model phi-total was (project file). Defined subgroup, mixed evidence.

scores.reason: The 2023 international hyperinsulinism guideline (Rec 1.1 Grade 1, moderate, per project file) and PES 2015 recommendations include insulin and C-peptide in the critical sample, backed by retrospective accuracy series (C-peptide above 291.5 pmol/L: sensitivity 82 percent, specificity 99 percent, single centre; C-peptide 1.55 vs 0.11 ng/mL). The guideline calls insulin and C-peptide criteria less definitive than BOHB, FFA and glucagon response, and insulin was undetectable in 5 of 28 confirmed cases. No trial. Measure type: insulin and C-peptide during hypoglycaemia (critical sample).

scores.reason: BOHB, FFA and the glucagon response are the more reliable markers (ketotic hypoglycaemia vs congenital hyperinsulinism: glucagon rise of 30 mg/dL or more in 24 of 27 vs 0 of 30), and insulin is often below detection. Insulin and C-peptide are supportive and add marginally; C-peptide does carry high specificity in one series, so not 0.
sources: PMID 37454648 DOI 10.1159/000531766 abstract; Table 1 values per project file

scores.reason: Igls consensus (2018) and the 2021 IPITA report, plus registry data: in CITR islet-alone recipients (n=677) fasting C-peptide predicted absence of severe hypoglycaemia (ROC AUC 0.906) and the optimal outcome (AUC 0.845, cut point 0.33 nmol/L), and Igls grade tracked CGM time in range in 55 recipients. This is predictive and classification evidence for grading graft function, not evidence that C-peptide grading changes treatment or outcomes. Measure type: basal and stimulated (MMTT) C-peptide.
sources: usecases-verified.md row 10 (Igls 2018 PMC5867272 full text per project skeptic)

scores.reason: Alternatives are HbA1c, insulin dose, severe-hypoglycaemia history and CGM, which Igls uses alongside C-peptide. In insulin-treated recipients C-peptide is the only direct marker of graft secretion, useful in a defined subgroup, but no analysis of incremental value over HbA1c, insulin dose and CGM (C-statistic, NRI) was found. Low sensitive-assay C-peptide is of questionable significance and kidney dysfunction raises levels (project file). Igls 2.0 not found.

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Prospective study or trial of C-peptide-guided insulin de-escalation in adults with doubtful type, reporting glycaemic control and ketoacidosis safety, with a harmonised random C-peptide cutoff by concurrent glucose.
path_to_viability.basis: Only consensus text plus accuracy and retrospective data were found (PMID 23413806, PMID 24843502); no outcome study of stopping insulin.

path_to_viability.missing_piece: External validation of C-peptide or UCPCR thresholds in a US multiethnic population plus a prospective pathway study of genetic-test yield and treatment change versus clinical criteria alone.
path_to_viability.basis: Thresholds derived in UK cohorts (PMID 21270186, PMID 23289766); calculator update validated externally in a UK population cohort (PMID 41086125); PPV 20 percent of antibody-negative UCPCR-positive pathway (project file).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Diagnostic accuracy cohort of the full hypoglycaemia panel (insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, BOHB, broad secretagogue screen including newer agents) in unselected adults with Whipple triad, with rapid turnaround drug screen.
path_to_viability.basis: Guideline rests on low-quality evidence (PMID 19088155) and the project file states no accuracy data were retrieved; screen may miss newer agents.

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Multi-centre, multi-ethnic prospective validation of the post-DKA C-peptide cutoff (fasting above 0.33 nmol/L or glucagon-stimulated above 0.5 nmol/L) against sustained insulin independence, with a defined withdrawal protocol.
path_to_viability.basis: Evidence is largely one research network (PMID 17130187, PMID 14602731) with an outcome defined by the same test; no guideline found.

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Validation of the 0.6 ng/mL fasting C-peptide criterion against clinical insulin dependence outside Japan, and adoption of the entity by a US or international body.
path_to_viability.basis: Criterion is a national expert definition (PMID 38184802); abstract gives no derivation; supporting cohorts are Japanese (PMID 40509916, PMID 38451108).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Incremental-value analysis (C-statistic, NRI, calibration, decision curve) of OGTT C-peptide over antibody count, OGTT glucose, age and BMI in existing TrialNet data, with a reduced-sample protocol.
path_to_viability.basis: DPTRS and Index60 are already built on TrialNet and DPT-1 data (PMID 22547092, PMID 35998266), but no incremental analysis of C-peptide alone was found and one 57-person model found AUC C-peptide not significant (PMID 39992257).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Multi-centre diagnostic accuracy study of insulin and C-peptide thresholds against BOHB, FFA and glucagon response using harmonised, low-range-validated paediatric assays.
path_to_viability.basis: Insulin undetectable in 5 of 28 confirmed cases (PMID 26490124); C-peptide threshold from one retrospective centre (PMID 39360602); guideline calls insulin criteria less definitive (PMID 37454648).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Igls 2.0 consensus with numeric, assay-specified C-peptide thresholds and CITR-based validation of incremental value over HbA1c, insulin dose and CGM.
path_to_viability.basis: Igls 2018 gives no numeric threshold for clinically significant C-peptide (project file); CITR data already exist (PMID 36657975); symposium proposed refinements (PMID 34061967).

anchor_issues: Row 3 D2: a GRADE guideline backed by low or very low quality evidence fits neither anchor 2 (observational) nor anchor 3 (consensus backed by studies); chose 2 because the guideline evidence for the insulin/C-peptide component is low quality and the discriminating test is the drug screen.
Row 3 D8: unclear whether to score added value against the drug screen (alternative test for the sulfonylurea question) or against clinical history; chose the drug screen as the main alternative.

Row 47 D2: a national expert diagnostic criterion (Japan) with no stated derivation is neither a guideline backed by studies nor mere opinion; chose 2 under the national-criteria logic of clarification 6 and the surrogate logic of clarification 8.

Row 10 D2: the decision is grading graft function (classification), not a treatment change; D2 anchors do not say whether prediction of outcomes by C-peptide counts as decision-impact evidence; scored 3 on consensus plus registry data and flagged that decision impact is not shown.

Row 4 D2/D8: the measurement (insulin, C-peptide) sits inside a bundle with BOHB, FFA and glucagon; D2 scored for the bundle's guideline backing, D8 scored for insulin and C-peptide alone against the other critical-sample markers.

Rows 32 and 31 D8: when C-peptide defines the reference outcome (beta-cell function), accuracy studies are circular, so anchor 19 data requirement cannot be met cleanly; chose 3 for row 32 with low confidence and 2 for row 31.
Row 49 D8: the mixed measure (OGTT glucose plus C-peptide, DPTRS/Index60) cannot isolate C-peptide's incremental contribution; scored the use as defined (post-load glucose plus C-peptide).
assumptions: Content of full-text sources (Holt 2021, Jones 2013, ADA Standards 2026, PMDI 2023, HI guideline 2023, PES 2015, Igls 2018, Galderisi 2025, Sims 2026) was taken from usecases-verified.md; I read abstracts only and the read level is stated per source.

Row 31 population read as adults on insulin with doubtful type or clinical T1D for 3 years or more, as in the row; de-escalation decision treated as the secondary decision, classification as the primary one.
Row 3 scored on insulin and C-peptide as the measure (the row text), not on the drug screen.
Setting tags: row 3 and 4 inpatient or procedural (hypoglycaemia evaluated during a spontaneous or supervised episode); row 32 specialist outpatient (testing weeks to months after DKA).
PubMed abstracts that were truncated by the fetch tool were treated as read only to the truncation point.
